priorities.finding: Only request-context features show a positive aggregate primary lift (+0.00221) with full coverage and positive daily lift on all four holdout dates. Within-user discrimination is stronger than top-five quality: cold-user GAUC is 0.654 versus nDCG@5 of 0.492, and warm-user/item GAUC is 0.631 versus nDCG@5 of 0.508. The positive direction is consistent, although lift magnitude is variable.
priorities.recommended_action: Fund request_context for the next experiment and stop feature expansion under the strict early-stopping rule. Diagnose or optimize top-five ranking separately rather than treating the GAUC signal as strong top-five evidence.

avoid: Reject user_profile, historical_user_author_affinity, upload_recency, content_duration, item_metadata, historical_author_response, and historical_item_response; each has negative aggregate primary lift or materially degraded ranking metrics: screen:user_profile, screen:historical_user_author_affinity, screen:upload_recency, screen:content_duration, screen:item_metadata, screen:historical_author_response, screen:historical_item_response.

Do not use current-impression outcome features such as feature:is_click, feature:is_comment, feature:is_follow, feature:is_like, feature:long_view, or feature:play_time_ms because they are unavailable at ranking time.
metric_diagnosis: The screening supports one budgeted direction only: screen:request_context. Its positive daily sign provides the best available within-user ranking evidence, but the daily standard deviation (0.00580) exceeds the mean lift (0.00221), so the effect should be validated with a subsequent temporal experiment. GAUC consistently exceeds nDCG@5 across cold-user and warm-user/item segments, indicating better broad ranking discrimination than top-five precision; no weakest-segment evidence was supplied, so segment-specific rejection beyond this diagnosis is not justified.
